chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by late dialogical frame and pastoral/institutional admonition about reprimand, anger, and repentance. Only one paragraph (¶9) presents a self-contained cosmological mechanism (the heavenly light-givers displaying two aspects to purify the soul/powers), which fits the older correspondential-cosmological substrate. A Matthean saying (Mt 6:21) appears in ¶10, marking Christian overlay.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong hagiographic/dialogue container: “Once again…”, disciple address and petition (“I beseech you…”), biographical/apostle framing; content is situational community counsel, not systematic cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Continuation of the disciple’s first-person question/argument within the dialogue scene; lacks cosmological architecture and functions as part of the Q&A setup.
Explicit petition formula (“So, now I beseech you, my master…”) and anxiety about personal sin—dialogue frame + application voice rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

Although introduced by a dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle speaks…”), the paragraph’s substance is disciplinary counsel about rebuke, shame, repentance, and managing a ‘brother’—cosmos is not being mapped; this is community-instruction material.
Extended ethical taxonomy of ‘evil anger’ (pride, cursing, retaliation, refusing judgement). This is moral/communal guidance without cosmological correspondential mechanism.
Directly practical instruction about handling obdurate persons and defining ‘strong reprimand’ that leads to repentance—pastoral discipline register.
Didactic simile of the wise doctor using hot/cool remedies; a rhetorical analogy applied to correction, not a systematic internal cosmology mapping layer.

Application-heavy expansion: rebuke/humbling word, correcting ‘brother’ with love/fear, fear leading to repentance. Institutional interpersonal focus indicates later pastoral use of correspondential language.

paragraphs.core_text: For the light-givers that are in the heavens shall be revealed with these two aspects, in the aspect of love and the aspect of fear. They display these two aspects of the powers above that are in the heavens, because of their soul that passes through the totality. For in these two appearances, the aspect of love that is beauty and sublimity, together with the other aspect of confrontation that is in them, they shall purify in them the powers above.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanism: heavenly ‘light-givers’ manifest paired aspects and effect purification of soul/powers through cosmic process (“passes through the totality”). This stays within the cosmic system (heavens/light-givers/powers), unlike the surrounding community admonitions.

Contains a Gospel/NT import (Mt 6:21: heart/treasure saying) embedded in exhortation (“you too…”). Even without an explicit citation formula, the identifiable NT entry-vector makes the paragraph Christian overlay.
Closing dialogue response and affirmation (“When that teacher heard… he said…”), typical frame closure/praise of the master’s lesson rather than teaching substrate.
